idiom_name: framework lifecycle contracts: Angular lifecycle hooks, NestJS container-managed providers
implementation_notes: TypeScript's framework ecosystem supplies the inversion as typed contracts: Angular calls lifecycle hooks such as ngOnInit and ngAfterViewInit on components and services, and Nest's IoC container instantiates providers, injects their constructor dependencies and invokes guards, interceptors and pipes at defined points around a request. The classic skeleton is replaced by a decorated class implementing a framework interface, which is why such classes contain almost no control flow of their own. The plain JavaScript form - a typed event listener or middleware function - remains the lighter option when no container is involved.
pitfalls: Lifecycle hooks run at framework-chosen moments and may run more than once (or not at all for a view that is never attached), so initialization must be idempotent.
Decorator support is a compiler feature: tsconfig settings such as experimentalDecorators change how metadata is emitted, and losing them breaks dependency injection only at runtime.
